name: Erdosteine

overview.mechanism: A mucoactive agent with antioxidant activity, evaluated as add-on therapy in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. [[ERDO-RESTORE]]
uses: Studied as an adjunct to usual COPD therapy to reduce exacerbations; verify local indications and treatment duration. [[ERDO-RESTORE]]

evidence.title: RESTORE: benefit driven by mild exacerbations

paragraphs.text: RESTORE was a 12-month randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in COPD; its prespecified intention-to-treat population included 445 patients. Added to usual treatment, erdosteine reduced total exacerbations from 1.13 to 0.91 per patient-year. The effect was driven by mild events; moderate/severe exacerbations were not significantly reduced.

Mean exacerbation duration was shorter (9.55 versus 12.63 days). There was no improvement in St George’s Respiratory Questionnaire score or time to first exacerbation, and the proportion reporting adverse events was similar between groups. These findings do not establish mortality benefit or replacement of usual COPD treatment.
RESTORE assessed respiratory outcomes; it did not establish renal dosing, dialysis use or protection from kidney injury.

sources.citation: Effect of erdosteine on the rate and duration of COPD exacerbations: the RESTORE study. PubMed PMID: 29025888.

draft_notes: No renal regimen inferred; local product label and organ-impairment contraindications remain verification gaps.
